engagement_title: The Halden Diaries season two kit: bring eight differently lit episodes to one channel look, recover the wordmark off the painted desk board, cut the season recap tall and wide, and rebuild the patron postcard the printer made last year into a live eight card run
vertical: Music, Film, Publishing and Media. Independent daily vlog channel entering its first sponsored season, self shot, self edited, patron supported, based in Portland, Maine
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post from a creator who films their own day to day content and needs recurring per episode post production, quoted in the ledger's grounding_note. The literal ask names basic colour correction, supporting graphics for lower thirds and end screens, 4K capture delivered as web ready 1080p, the supporting custom graphics wanted as their own deliverables, and an ongoing episode to episode collaboration rather than a one off. Two things in that post do not survive contact with the connector and are therefore re carved rather than pretended: on screen text burn in and lower third compositing do not exist here, so the supporting graphics become an authored editable end plate and caption plate set that the creator edits himself each week, which is closer to what the post actually wanted (graphics he keeps) than a burned in overlay he would have to re commission. The episode to episode consistency half of the post is the real commission and it is fully doable: one house look across eight differently lit episodes, one recovered wordmark, one recap in two aspects, and the printed patron card the post's real world equivalent creator sends out at season end. The creator handle is laundered to a fully invented persona, The Halden Diaries, wordmark HALDEN, tagline an ordinary week filmed, run by fictional creator Nate Halden. No real person, channel, sponsor or platform account is referenced.
client_one_liner: Eight episodes are locked and they do not look like one channel, my logo only exists as a painted board behind my desk, and the patron cards have to be at the printer in three weeks.
client_brief:
The Halden Diaries, season two kit

I film my own week and put out an episode every Sunday. Eight episodes are cut and locked for season two, and these are the first ones with a sponsor attached, so this is the first time the look matters to somebody other than me.

The honest state of things. I shoot in the kitchen, at the desk by the window, and out on the evening walk, and I shoot whenever the light happens to be there. Line the eight up and they do not look like one channel. Some are cold. The kitchen ones are orange. One is just brighter than everything else. I want the eight episode pictures to read as though they came off the same channel, and I want them to still look like my flat and not like a studio.

I need a short recap of the season for the top of the channel page, and the same recap again tall for the phone feed. My voiceover for it is recorded but it is rough, and there is a fridge in it somewhere.

My patrons get a set of printed cards at the end of every season, one card per episode. The printer did last year's set for me and I still have the file they printed from. I need the same card for these eight, each with its own picture, its own date and its own title.

The channel name only exists as a painted board that hangs behind my desk. I have never had a file for it. I need it as artwork, because it has to go on the cards and on the end plate.

And I need an end plate and a caption plate I can change myself every week, because the episode number moves and I am not paying somebody for that.

It should feel like an ordinary week filmed well. Warm, unhurried, a bit lived in. Not slick and not a brand.
price_band_and_audience: Sponsorship tier lifestyle vlog, patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set at season end, audience 24 to 38 and loyal rather than large. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up and the work becomes a studio channel: crushed contrast, a cool graded look, a hard geometric plate, a logo that sits large. That look reads as an agency production, it contradicts the whole premise of one man filming his own week, and the audience that pays 6 dollars a month for intimacy reads it as the channel having been bought. Push it down and it becomes a phone edit: no consistent white point, a caption plate in a default system face, a card that looks like a home printer job, which fails the sponsor who is paying for the season and fails the patrons who paid for a physical object. The correct register is domestic warmth held to a professional standard: one white point, one black point, real licensed type, restrained plates, and a wordmark that still looks hand painted because it was. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed with a per season retainer attached.

brand_identity.sector: Independent daily vlog channel, self shot and self edited, patron supported, entering its first sponsored season.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, Portland, Maine, a one person channel run entirely by its creator Nate Halden.
brand_identity.about: The Halden Diaries is a self shot, self edited vlog in which Nate Halden films an ordinary week in his own flat and puts out one episode every Sunday. The channel promises intimacy over production: the same rooms, the same face, the same unhurried attention week after week. Season two is its first with a sponsor, and the whole point is that the sponsor changed nothing about how the week feels.
brand_identity.audience: Loyal rather than large, aged 24 to 38, patrons who pay 6 dollars a month for closeness and receive a printed card set at each season end. They buy the feeling of a friend filming his week, not a studio production.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set mailed at season end, first sponsored season attached. Sits deliberately between a phone edit and a studio channel: domestic warmth held to a professional standard.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a warm humanist serif with a hand set feel that echoes the painted board. Text: a quiet, readable humanist sans. Nothing geometric and nothing slick. The type should feel set by hand at home rather than commissioned from an agency.
brand_identity.voice: First person, plain, unhurried, a little self deprecating. He writes the way he talks to camera. Example line: 'An ordinary week, filmed. Thanks for staying with it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand files have ever existed. The channel name lives only as a board Nate hand painted on limewashed pine before the first episode, one deep ink with a painted hairline rule beneath it, and it survives only as a handheld photograph. The wordmark HALDEN has to be recovered from that photograph as usable artwork. There is no logo file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Intimacy and honesty: one man filming his own week, kept that way even with a sponsor in the room.

assets_supplied.name: halden_s2_episode_masters/ (8 video files, mixed)
assets_supplied.kind: The eight locked episode cuts, exported by the creator himself over four months.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All eight, locked, nothing more will change in them. They are 4K off the camera."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: He is framed hard to the right of centre in the five desk episodes because the window is on his left, so a centred vertical crop takes the window and leaves him at the edge or out of frame entirely, while the resize still returns exactly the requested dimensions and reports success. Episode six is not a 4K export at all but a 1080p re render he made when his drive filled, which no filename or folder note reveals.

assets_supplied.name: halden_s2_stills/ (8 frame grabs)
assets_supplied.kind: One still per episode, pulled by the creator from his own timeline to stand as the episode's picture.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture per episode. The kitchen ones are orange, I know."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the eight are not frame grabs from the masters but screenshots of his editing window at desktop scale, so they sit far below the postcard picture box and cannot reach it except by interpolation, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside its own returned tradeoff record. Separately the evening walk still puts his shoulder at almost the luminance of the dusk sky behind it.

assets_supplied.name: halden_recap_vo.wav
assets_supplied.kind: The season recap voiceover, recorded by the creator across two sittings a week apart.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My voiceover for the recap. It is rough. There is a fridge in it somewhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The first sitting was recorded on a lavalier and the second on the camera's onboard microphone from across the room, so speech cleanup brings the two halves to two different presences rather than one, and the join sits mid sentence where neither half sounds wrong on its own.

assets_supplied.name: halden_patron_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer used for last season's patron card set, a landscape card with a picture box, an episode title line, a date line, a short standfirst and a channel URL along the foot.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The file the printer worked from last year. Same card, new episodes."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's front is a single continuous text flow, so the structure readout that drives the field mapping reports a story that silently omits one of its runs while keeping that run's line break, leaving the string well formed and every offset past it short by exactly that run's length, and the validator still calls the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: halden_desk_board.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the hand painted wooden board that hangs behind the creator's desk, the channel name lettered in one deep ink on pale limewashed pine, with a painted hairline rule beneath it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the name exists. I painted it before the first episode."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The lettering carries enclosed counters and background removal cannot punch an enclosed interior, so that route hands back a filled slab, and a prompt naming the board rather than the paint pulls the selection to the plank. The paint and the pine also run close in value along the right third where the desk lamp falls off.

assets_supplied.name: halden_episode_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the eight episode titles, their publish dates, a one line standfirst each, and the channel URL exactly as it must appear.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Titles and dates as they went out. The URL has to be exactly that."

acceptance_bar: Laid out in a row the way a channel page lays them, the eight episode pictures read as one channel: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one contrast handling. A picture that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The flat still reads as a flat. A treatment that turns a domestic kitchen into a studio fails even if the eight match each other perfectly.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, and no crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A picture that reaches the card's box by being enlarged fails.
The vertical recap keeps him in frame for its whole length, not only at its first second. A vertical that returns the right dimensions with the subject at the edge is not delivered.
The recap's audio reads as one person in one room. A join where the voice changes distance mid sentence fails.

The patron card set is one press ready file with one page per episode, eight pages in the order of the episode list, each page carrying its own episode's picture, title, date and standfirst, and no record standing in for another.
Every field on the card is present on every page, including the URL along the foot, and the URL reads exactly as supplied.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as the painted board at the size it actually reproduces on the card foot and on the end plate.

The end plate and the caption plate arrive in one working file he can edit, each keeping its own canvas size, with the words as text he can retype and the wordmark as live vector shapes rather than a picture of a layout, delivered alongside the self contained source they were built from.
One type system across the plates and the card, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states, per episode picture, what was applied and why that one differs from its neighbours, plus every resize any tool reported, what happened to the voiceover, and anything he should know about using the recovered mark.

adobe_surfaces.role: The whole moving half of the season kit. The summariser is how the agent finds where the usable moments actually sit across eight locked cuts it did not make, the quick cutter is the only shortening instrument available and it chooses its own moments inside whatever it is given, the resizer produces the vertical without ever adding a pixel, and speech cleanup has to reconcile two recording sittings that were never going to sit together. Every one of these returns a plausible looking artifact whose correctness is only visible by watching or listening to it.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Fixes one channel look and drives all eight episode pictures toward it one call at a time under three different domestic lighting regimes, cuts the card picture boxes and the plate crops without enlarging anything, and recovers the wordmark at paint level off a photographed pine board with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (including its validator mode), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the printer's flat press PDF into a live eight record merge with a per row picture binding, then renders the press file and the per record proofs. This is the only surface in the connector that produces a genuine one record per page print run, and the client's card is exactly that shape.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The end plate and the caption plate as one native editable document at two canvas sizes, which is what makes the weekly edit his job rather than a recurring invoice. Every picture must be pulled down and embedded as image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the wordmark goes in as inline vector so it stays editable, and family and weight are declared on every text element or the type falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed type system carrying the card and both plates. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on lived in rather than studio slick. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the entire kit, and the CSS has to use the returned slug.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The card is a genuine one record per page print run and belongs on the merge surface; the two plates have to be free form fixed canvases he can edit, which only the authoring surface produces. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline. Forty artifacts later the agent still has to know which URL is episode six.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eight episode stills and read their true pixel dimensions against what the card's picture box and the plates actually need.
trajectory.judgement: The creator says these are frame grabs. The files are the only thing that can settle whether they all are, and a picture that cannot make the box has to be found now rather than at the printer.
trajectory.produces: A per still triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast against the ground, and true dimensions against every destination.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one channel target from the best lit still and bring each of the eight toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good pictures, and it has to keep the flat looking like a flat. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for kitchen tungsten, window daylight and evening dusk. The agent holds one destination and reaches it by three different routes.
trajectory.produces: Eight graded stills at source scale with a per still parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections where a whole frame move breaks something, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate. Naming the room pulls the selection to the room. The kitchen frames need the tungsten pulled without taking the skin grey, and the dusk frame needs its sky held without flattening him into it.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have gone wrong.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the painted board: a paint level selection naming the lettering's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the plank, which polarity to trace, and whether the flat single colour mark or a colour accurate plate is what the card wants. Background removal is the wrong instrument on lettering with enclosed counters.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Cut the card picture boxes and the plate crops, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff record is the only channel that reports what a crop did to the dimensions, and it carries no warning language of any kind.
trajectory.produces: Eight card pictures and the plate crops, each with its returned tradeoff record captured.

trajectory.action: Clean the recap voiceover, then listen to it end to end rather than to its first ten seconds.
trajectory.judgement: Cleanup normalises noise, not distance. Two sittings recorded on two microphones a room apart do not become one voice because the hum is gone, and the response says nothing about it.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned voiceover with a written note on what the cleanup did and did not reconcile.

trajectory.action: Summarise the eight episode masters to find where the season's usable moments actually sit, since the agent did not cut them and cannot scrub them.
trajectory.judgement: Eight locked cuts made by somebody else are opaque. The summaries are the only map, and they are what makes the choice of source for the recap a decision rather than a guess.
trajectory.produces: A per episode content map and a shortlist of which episodes carry the recap.

trajectory.action: Cut the wide recap with the shortening cutter, then produce the vertical from it with the resizer, which never adds pixels.
trajectory.judgement: The cutter only shortens and picks its own moments inside what it is handed, so what it is handed is the real decision. The vertical is a reframe of a wide frame, which means something in that wide frame is being thrown away, and which thing depends on where he is standing.
trajectory.produces: A wide season recap and a vertical companion, both with their returned dimensions and durations recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 6 dollar patron tier and a lived in register rather than a studio one. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF to a working document, export its interchange form, and read the real frame inventory it actually contains.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anybody's control. Whether the card's front is four separate frames or one continuous flow decides whether fields are mapped per frame or by position inside a single story, and looking is the only way to find out.
trajectory.produces: A converted template plus a written inventory of its real text and picture frames with their bounds.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping readout for the converted template, compose the field mapping for title, date, standfirst, URL and the per row picture, run it back through the validator, and prepare the merge template.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping is offset work inside somebody else's document, and the validator's verdict is a statement about the mapping's shape, not about whether it points at the right characters.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template and the validator's response.

trajectory.action: Merge the eight records with the per row picture binding, render the press file and the per record proofs, and read the pages.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to record count is necessary and not sufficient. Multi record raster output comes back in an order the labels misreport, so identity is confirmed on the page rather than from the response.
trajectory.produces: An eight page press file, per record proofs, and a page by page identity check.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the end plate and the caption plate at their own canvas sizes, embed every picture as image data, place the wordmark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is exactly what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how quiet the plates can be and still carry a sponsor.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvas two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit of the second.

trajectory.action: Write the note: per still what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what the voiceover cleanup reconciled and what it did not, the card run's page by page identity, and how to use the recovered mark.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable that keeps him from re commissioning this next season, so it has to name the things that cannot be fixed as plainly as the things that were.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the vertical recap still has him in it. The resizer returns exactly the requested vertical dimensions and reports success, and the first frame looks correct, because a reframe of a wide shot has to discard most of the width and the tool takes that decision itself. He is framed hard to the right of centre through the desk episodes because his window is on his left, so what the vertical keeps is the window. Nothing in the response, the dimensions or the duration reports it, and the wide recap it came from is entirely correct. It is visible only by watching the vertical through, and which stretches of it are wrong depends on which episodes the cutter chose to draw the recap from, which the agent also only learns by running the cut.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the reframe is the last video step by necessity and the tool exposes no framing control, so a competent agent cannot do it right first time without already knowing where he stands in footage it did not shoot. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the recap again tall for the phone feed and says nothing about where he sits in frame. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different route entirely: re cut the wide recap from a different set of source episodes whose framing survives a centred reframe, or accept that some episodes cannot go vertical and rebuild the vertical from the ones that can.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re read the episode content maps for framing rather than content, re cut the wide recap from a different selection of sources, re derive the vertical from that cut, and watch it through before it is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A vertical recap delivered at exactly the right dimensions in which the creator is at the edge of frame or absent, published to the feed that carries the sponsor.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the field mapping actually points at the characters it names. The card's front is one continuous flow, and the readout that drives the mapping reports a story that silently omits one of its runs while keeping that run's line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns a valid verdict with no warnings on the wrong offsets, and preparing the template returns a success message while quietly dropping the mappings that no longer land. Which run is omitted, and therefore which fields survive, is a property of this specific document and is reported nowhere. It is discoverable only by round tripping the prepared template and looking for each expected placeholder in its own story text.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) A careful agent cannot dodge it by ordering or by care, because both signals it has (the validator and the prepare response) affirm the work; the only way through is to distrust a readout that nothing has flagged. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the printer used this file and asks for the same card with new content. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file itself and recompute every offset against that, which is a different source of truth, not the same call again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the offsets from the document's own reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, and re export it to confirm every expected field is present before a single record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight patron cards printed and mailed with the standfirst and the channel URL missing from every one of them, after every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the plate the whole caption look rests on. The caption plate is a soft translucent band the words sit on so they stay readable over any frame, and the natural constructions for that are a blurred backdrop or a layered soft shadow. The importer discards a blur outright, drops a backdrop treatment to its underlying flat fill, and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, all at a successful response with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports which of those happened, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the caption canvas can be checked no other way. Whether what survives still holds the words legible over a bright kitchen frame is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives this importer, which no response and no checklist enumerates, and no ordering helps because the normalisation happens at import and import is the last step. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a caption plate he can change himself, not for a particular construction. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different upstream asset or a different construction: bake the softness into the picture before it is embedded, or reduce the plate to the single opaque treatment the importer keeps and re judge legibility against the brightest frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the plate around whichever construction survives, re export, and audit both canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard, then re check the words against the brightest episode picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A caption plate delivered as an editable file in which the words sit on nothing and go unreadable over the bright kitchen frames, on the canvas nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Halden season two episode pictures
deliverables.spec: Eight episode pictures brought to one channel look across kitchen tungsten, window daylight and evening dusk: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one contrast handling, with the flat still reading as a flat rather than as a studio. Every output at or below its source dimensions with the returned tradeoff record captured, and a per picture parameter log including one line on why each differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Season two recap, wide and tall, with cleaned voiceover
deliverables.spec: A short wide season recap for the channel page and a vertical companion for the phone feed, the vertical keeping the creator in frame for its whole length and reaching its dimensions without a single added pixel, delivered with the recap voiceover cleaned and a written statement of what the cleanup reconciled between the two recording sittings and what it could not.

deliverables.name: Recovered HALDEN wordmark
deliverables.spec: The hand painted channel name recovered from a photograph of a limewashed pine board as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, its counters open and its painted hairline rule intact, delivered as both a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, and holding at the size it actually reproduces on the card foot as well as on the end plate.

deliverables.name: Patron card run, season two
deliverables.spec: One press ready file of eight pages, one episode per page in the order of the episode list, each page carrying its own episode picture bound per record plus its own title, date and standfirst and the channel URL exactly as supplied, rebuilt from the printer's own flat artwork into a live merge template. Delivered with per record proofs whose identity is confirmed on the page rather than from the response labels.

deliverables.name: End plate and caption plate, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying both plates at their own canvas sizes, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the wordmark as real vector shapes, every picture carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and the caption plate holding its words legible over a bright frame. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: he edits the document weekly and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Handover note
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per episode picture what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the file it applied to, the card run's page by page identity check, what the voiceover cleanup did and did not reconcile, and anything he should know about using the recovered mark.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file, raster or video, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against the source named for it in the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscale entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoff records captured from every image and video call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The vertical recap is a true vertical aspect at or below source scale and its duration does not exceed the wide recap it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the width, height and duration of both recap files.

verifiers_auto.text: The patron card press file has exactly eight pages, one per episode, in the order of the supplied episode list.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the press file and read each page's title and date against the episode copy.

verifiers_auto.text: Every expected field placeholder is present in the prepared merge template's own story text before merging, including the standfirst and the channel URL.

verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and place the plate over the brightest frame in Express.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as an ordinary week filmed well at a 6 dollar patron tier, not as a studio channel and not as a phone edit.
verifiers_human.how: Judge grade, type scale, plate weight and card density against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every limitation is named as plainly as every fix.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which are moving, and which need an authored fixed canvas he can edit, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Whether the eight episodes are one channel. The creator believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the kitchen tungsten frames toward the target before the room stops looking like his kitchen, versus naming one as unmatchable.
Which episodes the recap is drawn from, chosen from summaries of cuts the agent did not make, and judged on framing as well as on content.
Whether a vertical is producible from a given source at all, or whether that source has to be swapped rather than reframed.
Whether the two voiceover sittings can be reconciled, and how to say so in the note when they cannot.

Selection wording on the painted board: naming the board takes the plank, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the lettering, and background removal on enclosed counters is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the card foot, judged at reproduction size on the actual stock rather than at full canvas.
Whether the converted card is mapped per frame or by position inside one story, which the document decides and not the agent.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a lived in register rather than a studio one, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How quiet the plates can be and still carry a sponsor. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense branded plate is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a young man in a kitchen. IDENTITY: these are this creator's own eight locked episodes, his own flat, his own face and his own hand painted board, and the wordmark has to be RECOVERED off that board rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different channel's logo and a regenerated kitchen is not his. SPEC: the patron card is a press file of exactly eight pages in the episode list's order with each record's own picture bound to it and a URL that must read character for character, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for, and the vertical recap has a hard no added pixels requirement. EDITABILITY: the two plates are defined by being editable, since the episode number moves every week and he explicitly will not pay for that. And the whole middle of this engagement is verification against material reality that only running produces: is he still in the vertical frame, did the mapping point at the right characters, did the caption plate's softness survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no invented one. VIDEO AND AUDIO: only the four permitted Premiere operations appear, media_summarize to read cuts the agent did not make, video_create_quick_cut which only ever shortens and is never asked to trim to a timestamp, video_resize which is never asked to enlarge, and media_enhance_speech. No on screen text burn in, no lower third compositing, no motion graphics, no format conversion and no per artboard export appear anywhere, which is exactly why the real post's overlay ask was re carved into an authored editable plate set. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The crop tool DOES enlarge up to a two times cap and reports it only inside its returned tradeoffs, which is why the no enlargement bar is checked against that record rather than asserted. The mark work rests on documented findings: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is verified, remove_background cannot punch enclosed counters and collapses on disjoint lettering, and vectorize emits no viewBox and an opaque full canvas path at index zero, so the hygiene the acceptance bar scores is hygiene no tool performs. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator mode, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with a per row image column bound through additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout are verified end to end; page count equal to row count is verified for PDF output. The mapping checkpoint rests on the verified lossy textContent finding, where a dropped run left every later offset short, the validator still returned valid, prepare still reported success, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed. Multi record raster order is documented as misreported, which is why identity is checked on the page. No variable QR, no bleed claim and no named press preset appear. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, images must be embedded because every external reference resolved to a placeholder, blur is dropped and layered shadow truncated to layer one at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, and the non standard numeric weight per family is why font_styles is mandatory. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no upscaling, no OCR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no vector render or vector merge, and no batch above twenty files.
